title: Clearing Act 1 in VAULT RAIDERS
author: pikush
selftext:
Hey folks! I’m a solo dev making VAULT RAIDERS, where turn based tactics meets roguelite deckbuilding.

I’ve had a lot of great feedback since first sharing the game, but there have been plenty of questions about mechanics and gameplay. So, I went ahead and made a video recording an Act 1 playthrough in normal difficulty with the starting class. 

I’d love to hear your thoughts if you get a chance to check out the link! and if you want to play Act 1 for yourself, you can download the free demo on Steam. 

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5255890/Vault\_Raiders/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5255890/Vault_Raiders/)

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/pikush please add a bit about how you used AI and what the development process looked like. A mention that AI was involved isn't enough. It needs dev details. Rule 4 exists so promotional posts contribute to the conversation about making games. We want to avoid the sub getting drowned in low effort promotion. If this isn't updated, it may be removed.

replies.author: pikush
replies.body:
For sure! In terms of AI usage, I developed an art pipeline that I talked about in another post, where I use Claude to drive codex (I find Claude’s “taste” much more reliable and consistent over months of development) for image gen, before using Tripo to develop 3D models which then get cleaned up in blender. 

Most of the game ideas start in a notepad for me. I will often scan text and images I’ve written by hand, and use that to expand my design bible. I then work with AI to develop first playable versions of features, and then to adjust features or game balance based on playtests (most of which I do on my steam deck). 

If anyone is curious about these aspects of development, or other aspects of the game, I’d love to talk about it more!

comments.author: Beneficial_Feed_2595
comments.body:
This looks fun. I’d play it. My biggest/only gripe is that the rooms themselves feel a little muddy. Because everything is a small size it doesn’t feel visually clear. But I like the flow of gameplay, and it looks fun enough I’d give it a try.

I just wish there was more personality. It all feels really… brown. I wish there was more of a sense of humor or grit, or emotion. Gameplay looks great, but the story/world feels completely generic. That’s my note.

replies.author: Beneficial_Feed_2595
replies.body: Oh, and I really don’t like the design of the card. I can’t easily see on my phone visually what they do. Tell Claude to make the images bigger so they fill the frame, and make sure that every photo conveys the action and is clearly that thing.

replies.author: Beneficial_Feed_2595
replies.body:
From a design perspective the ui is actually really strong, but the cards themselves need work, as do the environment. Right not the brightest point of the environment are the walls. That’s where my eyes go first. You want the focal point of the enviro to be clearly on the enemies/ cover. Also pick a different font for the card titles the block font is a vibe but it’s too thick and not reading clearly.

Just a graphic designers perspective

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body:
XCOM 2 Meets Slay the Spire. Both great games. So this game does have potential if nailed successfully. 

  
One issue I have is your game is lacking a proper tutorial. You have to remember there will be people who've never played these types of games before, so you need an actual interactive tutorial in the game teaching them the absolute basics of mechanics.   
  
1. A 30 minute video is not the approach, no one is going to watch a long video to learn how to play.  
2. And you do have a "tutorial" with those help windows that occasionally pop up.... But those are more like loading screen help tips because sometimes the messages pop up while the player is focused on other things. Which will lose their attention and cause frustration when they have to learn the game themselves.

comments.author: Maple-Syrup89
comments.body:
Looks pretty nice!

I have a tech demo of a fantasy based tactical strategy game I had been working on, and I know from experience this genre can be pretty hard. Animations and forecasting really make or break a lot of the gameplay and yours are looking pretty good!  Good atmosphere too.
